jobs.occupation: IMPACT PORTFOLIO MANAGER (Fairer Futures Programmes) (Projektleiter/in / Projektmanager/in)
jobs.description:
Overview:

Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.

For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. 

Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future.

Unit’s description and purpose: 

The Global Impact unit strengthens the Fairtrade system by driving institutional learning and effectiveness through robust monitoring and evaluation systems. We are the hub for the analysis and communication of high-quality data and information about Fairtrade and its impact, as well as supporting strategy delivery. The unit includes the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) team, which is the Fairtrade system’s hub for MEL which directly connects evidence to strategic decision for the Global Strategy, individual Fairtrade projects and global programmes, Standards, producer support, and more.

PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Role purpose: 

The Impact Portfolio Manager (Fairer Futures Programmes) is responsible for stewarding the MEL frameworks for several of Fairtrade’s global product programmes, the flagship programmatic vehicles through which Fairtrade delivers measurable impact for farmers and workers under its 2026–2028 Global Strategy. 

The manager will share responsibilities for a total of three programmes (cocoa, banana, coffee) with another manager, with product- and thematic-specific focus to be determined upon hire.

Working in close collaboration with Fairtrade Producer Networks, Global Product Teams, and the Digital Service Unit, the role ensures that both programmes are underpinned by robust, coherent, and actionable MEL, from framework design through data collection, reporting, evaluation, and learning. The position serves as one of Fairtrade International's primary MEL contact across programme discussions, representing the Global Impact unit in a system that spans FI, National Fairtrade Organizations, and Producer Networks. This role also contributes to the Global Impact unit's impact services offer, drawing on programme MEL expertise to identify and develop customized services for the Fairtrade system and external partners.

Main Responsibilities:            

- MEL Framework, Indicators, and Data Management. Steward and drive the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the Theory of Change and MEL framework for several of the Fairer Futures Programmes, working in close collaboration with Producer Networks and Global Product Teams. Steward the KPI and activity/output indicator set for both programmes, including maintaining metadata and monitoring data quality. Work with PN MEL staff, Global Product Teams, and where needed external consultants to ensure systematic consolidation of existing programme data and the design and implementation of regular data collection processes. Coordinate with the Information & Knowledge team on data cleaning, analysis, and visualisation.
- Stakeholder Engagement and Project MEL Alignment. Serve as Fairtrade International's primary MEL contact for the product-expert colleagues in Producer Networks and Global Product Teams, providing technical MEL guidance, supporting capacity on data collection and reporting, and ensuring programme MEL requirements are understood and operationalised across the system. Work with PNs to ensure that MEL frameworks for individual projects within both programme portfolios are aligned to the overarching programme frameworks, providing where capacity is available guidance and quality assurance at project inception and during implementation
- Reporting, Synthesis, and Learning. Lead the preparation of programme-level MEL reporting for programmes, synthesising data and evidence from across the programme portfolio into outputs that feed into the overall strategy reporting cycle. Facilitate learning processes within programmes, identifying evidence-based insights and working with Global Product Teams and PNs to support programme adaptation where warranted. Ensure programme MEL evidence and KPI data are appropriately integrated into the overall strategy MEL cycle in close coordination with the designated strategy MEL lead within the Impact Management team.
- Programme Evaluation. Lead the design, commissioning, and management of the programme evaluations. This includes developing evaluation questions in collaboration with PNs and Global Product Teams, overseeing evaluation partners, and ensuring findings are translated into actionable learning.
- Impact Services and External Engagement. Identify opportunities to offer MEL technical services to Fairtrade system organisations and external partners, drawing on expertise developed through the programmes. Contribute to the scoping, design, and pitching of impact services in collaboration with the Head, with a particular focus on programme MEL, data collection design, and evaluation. Participate actively in relevant system-wide working groups, representing the Impact Management team's MEL perspective on cross-organisational initiatives.

Other tasks that are consistent with the level and responsibilities of this post.

SKILLS REQUIRED:

Level of education: The position holder will have a Master’s degree or higher in development economics, econometrics, applied sociology, social sciences or another relevant field in management or natural sciences. 

Years of professional experience: A minimum of five years' experience in monitoring, evaluation, and learning, with demonstrable experience designing and managing MEL frameworks for multi-stakeholder projects or programmes. At least two years' experience working in or with stakeholders from the Global South, preferably in agricultural or commodity supply chain contexts. Experience in coffee and bananas is an advantage.

Language requirements: Fluency in English required. Professional proficiency in Spanish is a advantage. 

Job Specific Competencies/knowledge: 

- Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning
- Project and Programme Management
- International Development Expertise
- Stakeholder Management
- Planning and execution
- Data Collection Design and Management
- Evaluation Design and Commissioning
- Enhancing data-driven decision making
- Data Analysis (quantitative and qualitative)
- Data Reporting and Synthesis
- Capacity Building

Personal Qualities: 

- Cross-cultural communication
- Facilitation
- Rapid Learning
- Collaboration/Teamwork
- Customer Service
- Presentation Skills
- Relationship Management
- Evidence Collecting
- Flexibility
- Feedback sourcing

Software/Tools: 

- Microsoft 365 (Excel, Word, Outlook, Powerpoint, Teams, Planner)
- Kobo Toolbox (or similar survey design and implementation tools)
- Miro (or similar online whiteboarding tools)
- Canva (or similar graphic design tools)
- Claude.ai (or similar AI  tools)
- Toladata (or similar project monitoring MEL platform)
- Power BI (or similar business intelligence software)

TERMS AND CONDITIONS:

- This is a two-year full-time position within Fairtrade International.
- Location is at Fairtrade International offices in Bonn, Germany with the opportunity for hybrid work arrangements
- The office language is English.
- Salary as per the Collective Bargaining Agreement for the Wholesale and Foreign Trade Industries for North Rhine Westphalia Group 6a and over tariff payments starting from €5455 Gross per month
- Holiday Bonus and 13th salary  
- 30 days of holidays per year (for fulltime employees)
- Subsidised public transportation ticket
- Subsidised meal services
- Childcare cost subsidy 

Please note that Fairtrade International is strict on compliance with the required qualification criteria mentioned above, and only those candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

OVERVIEW:

Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.

For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. 

Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future.

 Unit’s description and purpose: 

Global Products, Programs and Policy (GPPP) provides leadership to the Fairtrade system with selected product, program and policy intelligence. To this end GPPP provides information, tools and strategic direction as the main outputs. 

GPPP facilitates and contributes to coherent implementation of strategic plans within the Fairtrade system. GPPP develops new ways of delivering Fairtrade’s intended impact in a changing business environment and risk context.

PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Role purpose: 

The Cocoa Manager is responsible for implementation of GPPP cocoa works based on work schedule agreed with the Senior Advisor Cocoa. The work will deliver measurable impact for farmers and workers under its 2026–2028 Global Strategy. 

The Cocoa Manager joins a team that works fluidly, sharing responsibilities across multiple workstreams supporting each other where the need is the greatest to achieve their objectives. The environment is dynamic and priorities can shift with external events impacting workplans.  

In addition to other duties the Cocoa Manager, working within GPPP cocoa, will  work in close collaboration with Producer Networks, National Fairtrade Organisations and the Fairtrade International Global Impact team responsible for Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning, to ensure the Fairer Futures Programme – West Africa Cocoa is implemented professionally and on time. The programme is primarily focused on increasing the household income of farmers who are members of Small Producer Organisaitons in the programme. The programme leads to farm level interventions through Small Producer Organisaitons including pruning, cocoa tree planting and shade tree planting among others. The programme includes further interventions on income such as Village Savings and Loans Association, and interventions on social compliance including increasing the effectiveness of child labour monitoring, reporting and remediation. 

Future working responsibilities may extend to other geographies and other commodities.

Main Responsibilities:            

- Supporting National Fairtrade Organisations, in their responsibilities to maintain and grow the market for Fairtrade cocoa.
- Supporting Producer Networks, in their work with Small Producer Organisations, and maintaining and growing the market for Fairtrade cocoa.
- Programme design. Work with stakeholders, and mostly importantly the Producer Network, to ensure programme design is based on evidence with robust monitoring, evaluation and learning contributing to the evolution of the programme.
- Programme implementation. Co-management with the Producer Network based on agreed reporting structures and formats providing oversight and reporting to stakeholders in a timely manner. This will include the running of, and reporting to, a working committee.
- Financial reporting.  Responsible for ensuring timely quarterly financial reporting including an understanding of any variance from plan and agreed actions to remediate that situation.
- Programme monitoring, evaluation and learning. Working with Fairtrade International monitoring, evaluation and learning experts and the Producer Network to ensure implementation and prioritisation of effective monitoring, evaluation and learning in a timely manner.
- External programme reporting. Working with Fairtrade International monitoring, evaluation and learning experts, Producer Network and National Fairtrade Organisations ensuring agreed reporting deadlines are met with quality reporting to be used with commercial stakeholders, government and other interested stakeholders.
- External stakeholder engagement, traders. Working closely with the Producer Network manage relationships with exporter, importer and processers of cocoa who purchase Fairtrade cocoa from Small Producer Organisaitons. Traders are a critical part of the supply chain and their incorporation into the programme is desired and necessary.
- External stakeholder engagement, events. Working with National Fairtrade Organisations you will be speaking at public and trade events on the strategic objectives of our work, the progress and impact with the aim of influencing the sector.
- External stakeholder engagement, media. Where required you will interact with media.
- Fairtrade Standards and Pricing. Liaising with the lead department in Fairtrade on standards and pricing, Fairtrade’s Standards Unit and Pricing Unit, you will be working on standards and pricing matters relating to Fairtrade’s cocoa work and the programme. 

This will include and not limited to consultations, queries and evolution of standards and pricing. 

Other tasks that are consistent with the level and responsibilities of this post.

SKILLS REQUIRED:

Level of education: The position holder will have an undergraduate degree in science or the arts. 

Years of professional experience: A minimum of three years' experience in complex project management which includes implementation in the global South and preferably West Africa.

Language requirements: Fluency in English and French required. Professional proficiency in Spanish is an advantage. 

Job Specific Competencies/knowledge: 

- Project and Programme Management
- People management, particularly where they are not under your direct management
- Stakeholder Management
- International Development Expertise
- Planning and execution
- Financial reporting
- Negotiation
- Public speaking
- Capacity Building

Personal Qualities: 

- Cross-cultural communication
- Facilitation
- Rapid Learning
- Collaboration/Teamwork
- Customer Service
- Presentation Skills
- Relationship Management
- Evidence Collecting
- Flexibility
- Seeking and action on feedback 

Software/Tools:

- Microsoft 365 (Excel, Word, Outlook, Powerpoint, Teams, Planner)
- Miro (or similar online whiteboarding tools)

TERMS AND CONDITIONS:

- This is a two-year full-time position within Fairtrade International.
- Location is at Fairtrade International offices in Bonn, Germany with the opportunity for hybrid work arrangements
- The office language is English
- Salary as per the Collective Bargaining Agreement for the Wholesale and Foreign Trade Industries for North Rhine Westphalia Group 6a and over tariff payments starting from €5455 Gross per month
- Holiday Bonus and 13th salary  
- 30 days of holidays per year (for fulltime employees)
- Subsidised public transportation ticket
- Subsidised meal services
- Childcare cost subsidy

Please note that Fairtrade International is strict on compliance with the required qualification criteria mentioned above, and only those candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

jobs.description:
Job Overview

ISR is accredited by the German authorities as an ‘Anerkannte Internationale Ergänzungsschule’ (International Supplementary School) and by the US accrediting agency Cognia (formerly known as AdvancED). ISR is an IB World School authorized to offer the IB Diploma Programme, and also offers Cambridge Assessment International Education (CAIE) IGCSE courses. The school is a certified member of the Council of International Schools (CIS).

We wish to hire a dedicated and qualified full-time Admissions Employee (m/f/d) to join our dynamic educational institution from Autumn, 2026.

The successful candidate should be outgoing, confident in communicating with a wide range of people and able to build positive relationships quickly. Strong interpersonal skills, a collaborative mindset and a flexible approach to work are essential. A general understanding of different school systems and educational pathways would be an advantage.

Key Roles and Responsibilities

- Proactively contact interested families, provide relevant information and identify their individual needs.
- Manage and respond to all incoming enquiries from prospective families in a timely and professional manner.
- Maintain accurate records in the admissions database and ensure consistent follow-up throughout the enquiry process.
- Conduct school tours during regular school operations and provide personalised guidance on ISR’s educational programs and school community.
- Support prospective families throughout the entire application and enrolment process.
- Represent ISR and present its educational concept at internal and external events.
- Attend and actively support the planning, coordination, and delivery of information sessions, open days, and Saturday Info Days.
- Build positive and trusting relationships with prospective families while ensuring a welcoming and professional experience at every stage

Qualifications

- Completed vocational training or a university degree.
- Previous experience in customer service, client advisory or sales.
- Excellent written and spoken English and German; additional language skills would be an advantage.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
- A professional, service-oriented and approachable manner.
- Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
- Flexibility, reliability and strong organisational skills.
- Strong IT skills, particularly in Microsoft Office applications.
- Experience with Veracross is an advantage

Job Benefits

We are looking for someone who can make an immediate impact in a fast-paced, dynamic, and rewarding working environment. In return, we offer a range of opportunities for professional growth and career development.

If you are enthusiastic, highly motivated, enjoy a challenge, and believe you can contribute to the continued growth and development of our new ISR Elementary School Düsseldorf, we would be delighted to hear from you.

As Head of Robotics & Drones (m/f/d)

... you will assume strategic and operational responsibility for establishing, developing, and scaling our business unit in the field of robotics and drone technologies. You will drive innovation, identify new market opportunities, and develop sustainable business models in a dynamic and technologically demanding environment.

Your Responsibilities:

- Developing and implementing a comprehensive business development strategy for the Robotics & Drones division.
- Identifying and evaluating new market potential, trends, and business opportunities.
- Establishing and maintaining strategic partnerships (e.g., technology providers, startups, industry partners).
- Responsibility for the commercialization of new products and solutions.
- Leading interdisciplinary projects from concept to market launch.
- Analyzing competitors as well as market and customer requirements.
- Collaborating with internal teams (e.g., Engineering, Sales, Marketing) to ensure optimal implementation of solutions.
- Developing go-to-market strategies and supporting the sales team.
- Leading and expanding a global, high-performing team in the Robotics & Drones division.
- Budget responsibility and reporting to senior management.

This job posting is for a full-time position (40 hours per week) at EJOT SE & Co. KG. The team meets weekly at our location in Bad Laasphe.

Your Experience - We'd love to meet you if you have the following qualifications:

- A bachelor’s or master’s degree in business, engineering, computer science, or a comparable qualification.
- Experience in business development, ideally in the fields of robotics, UAVs/drones, or automated systems.
- A proven track record of success in developing new business areas or products.
- A strong understanding of technological trends and innovations in the field of robotics and automation.
- Entrepreneurial thinking combined with strategic foresight.
- Experience leading teams and projects.
- A global perspective is essential for you: With approximately 6–8 trips per year, including to Asia and North America, you will actively shape international collaboration.
- Strong communication and negotiation skills combined with a confident demeanor in an international setting.
- Excellent German and English language skills round out your profile.

Why EJOT?

- The satisfaction of working for a well-established and financially independent family business.
- Freedom to exercise creativity, drive innovation, and bring your own ideas to life.
- Competitive compensation with attractive benefits and perks.
- State-of-the-art work environment, infrastructure, and communication technologies.
- Work-life balance thanks to flexible work schedules.
- Remote work options.
- Employee profit-sharing.
- Professional development opportunities.
- Workplace health management.

- Corporate Benefits

WE ARE HIRING

Attorney-at-Law (m/f/d)
Commercial Law (North Macedonian Law) – Full-time or Part-time (min. 30h/week)
Location: initially Dresden, Germany / prospectively North Macedonia

WHO WE ARE

At NAUTARIS. legal | tax, we are not a traditional law firm with dusty files and dictation. We are an international, digitally oriented team of over 60 lawyers, tax experts, and accountants across Germany, the Czech Republic, and Poland, delivering outstanding work. We provide holistic, practical, and forward-looking advice to businesses—both legally and tax-wise.

A particular focus of our work lies in international and cross-border matters. Looking ahead, we plan to establish our own office in North Macedonia at a central location (e.g., Skopje, Bitola, Ohrid, or similar). We see significant economic and legal potential there and aim to develop this location deliberately and responsibly, closely connected to our existing offices.

WHAT WE OFFER

- A strategically exciting position with an international perspective
- Thorough onboarding and close support during the initial phase
- An interdisciplinary and appreciative working environment
- Clear structures, short decision-making processes, and genuine trust
- The opportunity to actively help build and shape a new office location
- Long-term collaboration with development prospects
- Permanent full-time or part-time employment (min. 30h/week)
- Predictable and flexible working hours with electronic time tracking
- A modern, well-equipped workplace
- A strong team culture: shared breakfasts, team events, and celebrations that strengthen cohesion
- Further training opportunities through seminars, training sessions, and individual programs, even during the probation period
- Free beverages, massages, parking options, and attractive additional benefits such as a monthly tax-free non-cash benefit of €50

WHAT YOU BRING

- You are a fully qualified lawyer (advokat) with solid knowledge of North Macedonian law, with a focus on commercial law
- You are a well-rounded commercial lawyer, not narrowly specialized
- Ideally, you have 2–3 years of professional experience (not mandatory)
- Business-fluent German or English skills (one of the two is required), as well as openness to using translation tools in daily work
- A high willingness to travel between Germany and North Macedonia

What matters most is that you are open to new legal and economic topics and are able to familiarize yourself with international and cross-border legal matters, particularly EU law, private international law, and relevant treaties. In addition, you bring economic and organizational understanding, as well as enthusiasm for building structures and contributing entrepreneurially.

You work in a highly independent and structured manner and demonstrate integrity, discretion, and loyalty toward the firm and our clients. You communicate effectively, even across distances.

You think long-term and entrepreneurially and are able to find creative solutions to complex economic and organizational challenges.

YOUR PERSPECTIVE

- Your place of work will initially be in Dresden, Germany, for 1–2 years.
- During this time, you will gain a comprehensive understanding of our working methods, client structure, firm culture, and interdisciplinary collaboration with our tax advisory team.
- At the same time, you will be regularly involved in project-based work in North Macedonia.
- The experience and structures gained in Germany will be gradually and transformatively transferred to North Macedonia and will play a key role in establishing and supporting a new office there.
- The exact location will be determined jointly and is intentionally kept open.

YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

- Providing legal advice to companies in a business-oriented environment
- Advising under North Macedonian law in the field of commercial law in its full scope, in particular: - Corporate law (including company formations, restructurings, and dissolutions)
- Drafting and negotiating contracts
- Supporting location decisions and investment projects
- Employment law matters
- Interfaces with tax law in close cooperation with our tax advisors
- Advising on funding opportunities and business-related regulatory frameworks
- Supporting and actively shaping business processes
- Building, maintaining, and developing client relationships
- In the long term: co-establishing and independently managing a law firm office in North Macedonia in close coordination with the Dresden office
- Regular professional and organizational exchange with the German team

WE LOOK FORWARD TO HEARING FROM YOU

Are you interested in joining us on this journey of building a new office in North Macedonia and looking for a long-term position explicitly designed as an employment relationship? Then let’s talk.

Please send us your application documents, including your salary expectations and earliest possible start date, as a PDF to:
bewerbung@nautaris-legal.com

Ms. Sophie Kahl | sophie.kahl@nautaris-legal.com | +49 351 4383708 517
Ms. Marija Treneva | marija_treneva@yahoo.com

Farm Trans has been a force in food transport since 1987, and thanks to innovations and investments in IT, sustainability and our employees, we will remain one - for next-level logistics.

We are looking for passionate truck drivers (f/m/d) who want to work in the world of food!

Your main task with us is the transport of food (national & international), from fresh potatoes (unloading with walking floor, for example) to frozen products. To do this, you will need a CE driving license (Code 95) and knowledge of English and/or German.

We offer you:

• German permanent employment contract

• Good salary

• Active support for finding accommodation in Germany

• New work clothes

• Modern truck fleet (with modern and safe technology)

• Cultural diversity in the company

• Internal training through the Farm Trans Academy & mentoring

• Different working time models

• And much more

Would you like to work in a growing, stable and social company where you can immediately get a permanent contract? Then we would like to invite you to an introductory meeting! Apply via our website or by email to recruitment@farmtrans.com (recruitment@farmtrans.com) .

Our location in Nettetal, the lake town on the Lower Rhine, is located in the heart of the Maas-Schwalm-Nette international nature park on the German-Dutch border between the cities Düsseldorf, Duisburg and the border town of Venlo and impresses with excellent transport connections.

We welcome your application, regardless of age, gender and background.

Find out more at www.nettetal.de (http://www.nettetal.de) .

jobs.occupation: Senior Process Manager (d/f/m) R&D Operational Excellence & Process Improvement (Forschungs- und Entwicklungsingenieur/in)
jobs.description:
In this role, you will drive the efficiency of the global Stage-Gate process for product development across LIXIL's brands and regions. You are the operational engine behind our R&D delivery: ensuring clear work packages, disciplined gate transitions, and practical governance that project teams can easily adopt. As the primary subject matter expert, you will serve as the trusted advisor for project managers and gatekeepers on all process inquiries.

The role works through influence across a matrixed, multi-cultural organisation and is a service to colleagues rather than an audit function. R&D is in active transformation on tooling and data quality, so ambiguity and shifting priorities are part of the job.

Your Responsibilities:

- Drive continuous optimisation of the global Stage-Gate Work Packages, ensuring deliverables are lean, consistent and harmonised across brands and regions.
- Maintain and enforce the global R&D governance framework: processes, tools, RASCI models, cadence structures and compliance checkpoints.
- Safeguard gate readiness, documentation integrity and audit readiness across all gate transitions.
- Define, track and report R&D KPIs covering gate discipline, cycle time and pipeline health.
- Develop and maintain digitalized templates, blueprints, work instructions and process documentation that simplify execution for project managers.
- Coordinate cross-functional and cross-regional alignment, so local delivery conforms to global R&D standards.
- Ensure Stage-Gate documentation and gate data are captured consistently and kept current in the governing systems, and represent process requirements towards the system owners.
- Build and maintain the R&D Knowledge Hub as the single, topic-structured source for process documentation, templates and training material, curated as an ongoing exercise.
- Ensure data continuity between Stage-Gate governance and Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), acting as the business-side representative to translate process requirements into system specifications with the Global PLM team.

Your Profile:

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Business Management, Industrial Management or comparable.
- 7 to 10 years in process management, R&D project management or operational excellence, gained across more than one industry, ideally in product development or manufacturing.
- Proven implementation of Stage-Gate or comparable phase-gate models
- Working understanding of project and portfolio management systems used in an R&D environment (e.g. Planisware Orchestra, SAP) and good data literacy for KPI definition and process analysis.
- Interest in how AI, automation and digital tools can simplify product development processes.
- Solid understanding of PLM, ERP, and engineering change management systems (e.g., SAP, Planisware Orchestra), with the ability to align process governance with system architecture.
- Demonstrated comfort, curiosity and respect across cultures and working styles is a core requirement.
- Gives and receives feedback constructively.
- Lean, Six Sigma or comparable optimisation approaches an advantage.
- Strong moderation and stakeholder skills, able to steer cross-regional teams without direct reporting lines. Able to translate between technical detail and business framing.
- Business-fluent English required, German an advantage.

Our offer:

- A salary package that ties directly to your work experience and responsibilities
- Comprehensive health management, including an on-site fitness room, local and digital health services, Health Cashback, and Hansefit membership
- Diversity & Inclusion: We offer equal opportunities for all individuals and support your personal development
- Access to a wide range of employee benefits, such as discounts on travel, fashion, media, mobile phones, and more
- A highly motivated, appreciative, and international team that inspires you and offers opportunities to learn and grow
- A modern company restaurant to ensure your well-being during the day

Interested?

Then we are looking forward to your application!
